rules: Reading or writing any field in sstatus is equivalent to reading or writing the homonymous field in mstatus.
When MXR=0, loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed.
When MXR=1, loads from pages marked readable (R=1) or executable (X=1) will succeed.
When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) will fault.
When SUM=1, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) will be permitted.
SUM has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect or when executing in U-mode.
SUM is read-only 0 if satp .MODE is read-only 0.
When mstateen0 .CTR=0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrctl, vsctrctl, sctrdepth, or sctrstatus raise an illegal-instruction exception.

When mstateen0 .CTR=0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sireg* when siselect is in 0x200..0x2FF, or vsireg* when vsiselect is in 0x200..0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR=0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, execution of the SCTRCLR instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR=1 and hstateen0 .CTR=1, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state behave as described in Section 7.2 and Section 11.2, and SCTRCLR behaves as described in Section 11.3.1.
When mstateen0 .CTR=1 and hstateen0 .CTR=0, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state and VSmode execution of SCTRCLR raise a virtual-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR=1 and hstateen0 .CTR=1, when VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state, they behave as described in Section 7.2 and Section 11.2.
When hstateen0 .CTR=0, qualified control transfers executed while V=1 will continue to implicitly update entry registers and sctrstatus.
When an interrupt traps to S-mode, the SPP bit is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, or 1 otherwise.
When an SRET instruction is executed from a trap handler, the SPP bit is set to user mode if it was 0, or supervisor mode if it was 1, and then SPP is set to 0.
When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to SIE, and SIE is set to 0.
When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to SPIE, and SPIE is set to 1.

An interrupt i traps to S-mode if both (a) the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or (b) the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode, and (c) bit i is set in both sip and sie.
Interrupts to S-mode take priority over any interrupts to lower privilege modes.
